A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoPo research. All 23 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original SoPo experiments on HumanML3D and KIT-ML, synthetic simulations, component ablations, and generated-motion examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds text-to-image experiments, spatial-alignment evaluation, a user study, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The offline preferred motions, online unpreferred-motion sampling, threshold filtering, similarity weighting, diffusion objectives, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Applying SoPo to FLUX introduces another experimental application without documenting a redesigned algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 extends coverage beyond motion generation and synthetic simulations to text-to-image generation, using HPDv2-based preparation, FLUX-generated training pairs, and HPD evaluation (Appendix A.1). HumanML3D and KIT-ML remain, with an additional targeted spatial-alignment scenario.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds real-motion comparisons against offline DPO, online DPO, and their naive combination, substantially strengthening the practical controls beyond v2's synthetic comparison. Conversely, Fg-T2M and M2DM disappear from the HumanML3D benchmark table. Table 1's MoDiPO comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a Multimodal metric to the HumanML3D comparison and image-generation evaluation using five scoring models. Appendix A.3 introduces left/right-swapped reward tests and human assessment of 500 motions from 100 spatial prompts. These are additional evaluation designs; the retained motion experiments' principal settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test online/offline/combined training strategies (Table 5), sensitivity to C and beta (Table S2), reward-model versus generator spatial understanding, and human preferences associated with reward hacking (Figure 4). The existing objective, threshold, and sample-count ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 reports plus/minus values without specifying their statistical basis. v3's checklist identifies Table 1's intervals as based on 20 independent repetitions and adds uncertainty to previously unqualified PriorMDM and CrossDiff entries. This establishes additional reporting, not an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: v3 fills missing Top-1/Top-2 results, adds Multimodal scores, and reports new ablation, image-generation, spatial, and human-preference outcomes. Newly reported spatial accuracies are 0.632 for MLD and 0.764 with SoPo. Existing headline values, including MLD+SoPo's MM Dist of 3.185, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 2's Eq. (6) adds averaging over motion groups x1:K to the previous expectation over conditions c. The appendix proofs and derivations remain substantively unchanged, making this a localized revision to the formal statement.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about offline overfitting, online sampling bias, semi-online preference optimization, and motion-generation improvements. The added experiments do not redefine those principal claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation connecting better spatial discrimination by reward models to improved generation, interprets the additional sensitivity and strategy studies, and claims KL regularization helps avoid reward hacking (Section 5.3). The existing limitation concerning reward-model generalization remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds image-pair construction, LoRA rank 128/scaling 256, hardware information, and future code/data-release plans. It removes v2's explicit MDM learning rate of 10^-5 without specifying a replacement. Image-training cost is unreconciled: Appendix A.1 states 330 GPU hours, while Table S1 lists 32 for SoPo.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds motion-foundation-model positioning, while new Appendix D broadens discussion to differentiable rewards, reinforcement learning, personalized alignment, and DPO for video, 3D, and audio. Several earlier motion-generation references are removed. This substantially expands the research context while retaining MoDiPO as the closest motion-alignment work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. v3 moves experimental appendices ahead of implementation details and proofs, adds related-work and checklist sections, and makes localized heading, affiliation, acknowledgement, and language edits. The main narrative undergoes limited rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds spatial/user-study plots, an image-comparison grid, and strategy, image-result, and hyperparameter tables. It expands the HumanML3D table with a Multimodal column and relocates existing displays. Metric headers are misaligned with values in Tables 4, 5, and S2; the original supplementary motion figure is retained as Figure S3.

improvement.justification: The new practical DPO controls, spatial tests, and image experiments broaden validation beyond v2. However, v3 introduces misleading metric headers, unreconciled image-training costs, and an inadequately documented user study used to support its reward-hacking interpretation. The checklist also denies human-subject research despite the reported study. These gains and reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment of the net change in overall quality.
